title: Transformer equivalent
caption: The ideal turns ratio disappears only with consistent voltage bases on the two sides. Leakage impedance remains.

title: Referred impedance
caption: A single per-unit series impedance can replace the referred transformer equivalent.

title: An unbalanced phasor set
caption: Unequal magnitudes or unequal angular separations require component decomposition.

title: Three sequence phasor sets
caption: Read the phase labels: positive a-b-c, negative a-c-b, zero all coincident. The main text fixes a=1 angle 120 degrees.

title: A class one-line system
caption: Generator, transformers, line, breakers, buses and load are represented by one phase of a balanced three-phase network.

title: One-line symbol key
caption: Recognize generator, bus, transformer, circuit breaker, transmission line and load before drawing equivalent networks.

title: LG series connection
caption: All three sequence currents are equal. Neutral impedance 3Zn belongs inside Z0; the external phase fault appears as 3Zf, counted separately.

title: Finite-impedance LG network
caption: The return branch is 3Zf because the physical phase current is three times the sequence current.

title: LL connection and one-line location
caption: The positive and negative ports share their fault voltage; their network currents have opposite signs. Zero sequence is absent.

title: Solid LLG connection
caption: Positive sequence feeds the parallel negative and zero networks. Use the corrected current signs in Section~\ref{faultnumericals}; the diagram does not justify copying the erroneous source arithmetic.

title: Relay and breaker recognition
caption: The relay decides; the breaker interrupts the power circuit. They have different current ratings and functions.

title: Primary and backup arrangement
caption: The feeder device isolates its local fault first. The upstream device supplies delayed backup; settings depend on the actual installation.

title: Time grading
caption: The source illustration gives example delays. Coordination needs a margin covering breaker time, relay error and overtravel, not these exact universal settings.

title: Current grading
caption: Compare pickup and fault current along a radial feeder. Current grading alone fails where adjacent fault currents are too similar.

title: CT-relay-trip-coil circuit
caption: Follow the low-power sensing circuit separately from the DC trip supply. A relay contact energizes the breaker trip coil.

title: Overcurrent characteristic family
caption: Definite time, inverse, very inverse and extremely inverse curves describe operating time versus current multiple. Instantaneous still has finite operating time.

title: Current and voltage coils
caption: A directional element combines current and a polarizing quantity. An ordinary nondirectional overcurrent element need not have a voltage coil.

title: Forward and reverse fault phasors
caption: Direction depends on the polarizing-voltage/current relationship and relay characteristic angle, not current magnitude alone.

title: Directional induction construction
caption: Identify potential coil, current coil, moving disc and trip contacts. The configured torque direction defines forward operation; source prose must not be read as a universal reversed convention.

title: Distance sensing and processing
caption: The selected voltage/current loop estimates apparent impedance. Fault resistance, infeed and instrument errors affect the estimate.

title: Distance reaches
caption: The class 80/120 percent settings and delays are illustrative. Zone reaches must coordinate with neighbouring lines.

title: Overlapping protection zones
caption: CT locations define zone boundaries around breakers. This equipment-zone sketch is distinct from distance-relay reach zones.

title: Differential balance and internal fault
caption: With all currents referenced into the zone, their sum is approximately zero for through current and nonzero for an internal fault.

title: Pilot-wire differential circuit
caption: Trace CT secondary circulation during an external fault. Ideally no spill current flows through the operating coil.

title: Electromagnetic relay gallery
caption: These photographs provide recognition context. Attraction and induction are different mechanisms; the syllabus develops induction type.

title: Double-winding induction-disc construction
caption: Identify the two electromagnets, aluminium disc, spindle, spring, moving/fixed contacts and auxiliary winding connections.

title: Shaded-pole induction structure
caption: The copper shading ring delays one portion of the pole flux. Spatially and temporally displaced fluxes produce disc torque.

title: Watt-hour-meter induction structure
caption: The winding arrangement produces two phase-displaced fluxes through the disc. The permanent magnet supplies braking torque.

title: Induction-cup construction
caption: The light conducting cup rotates in the air gap around a stationary iron core. Multiple poles create the required flux interaction.

title: Static device gallery
caption: Electronic measuring circuits replace the moving measuring element. The output may still use an electromechanical auxiliary contact.

title: Static and directional static blocks
caption: The first diagram shows rectifier, measuring circuit, amplifier, output and trip supply. The second includes phase comparison for direction. Compare the clearly separated time-overcurrent and instantaneous diagrams in Section~\ref{digital}.

title: Instantaneous static chain
caption: Rectification/conditioning, comparison and output trigger replace the induction delay. A comparator reference determines pickup.

title: Digital relay recognition
caption: Front-panel controls and indication are interfaces; the protection computation occurs inside the device.

title: Basic microcomputer protection blocks
caption: Analogue input conditioning precedes A/D conversion; the digital processor performs the protection decision.

title: Original microprocessor flowchart
caption: Follow acquisition, pickup decision, delay, repeated current check, trip and reset. The main text adds explicit dropout handling and a clearer loop.

title: Historical 8085 overcurrent hardware
caption: This class design rectifies CT-derived voltages before multiplexing and A/D conversion. It estimates an overcurrent magnitude; do not claim this rectified waveform retains AC phase for a general phasor relay.

title: Sample-and-hold numerical hardware
caption: CT/VT signals are conditioned, sampled, multiplexed, converted and processed. Anti-alias filtering is explained in the main text.

title: Numerical relay signal and power paths
caption: Surge filtering and anti-alias filtering protect the analogue input; the processor runs protection logic and sends digital outputs and communications.
